svg.title: Keep the HTTP operation fixed; fill in values
svg.desc: Five steps read top to bottom for an Action on the built-in weave-http@2.0.0 connector. 1, the connection fixes the HTTPS origin, the authentication kind, secret handles by slot and the allowed destinations; the operator controls network policy, and endpoint and credentials stay outside input. 2, the published Action fixes the method, path template, parameters and statuses; the method sets the side effect and a write is never retried; schemas, byte limits and timeout are pinned; Studio and the CLI check it offline and publishing runs the checks again. 3, input fills only the declared path, query, header and JSON body values and cannot replace the origin, authentication or accepted statuses. 4, the native executor validates the input, checks authority, resolves scoped credentials, checks authority again, validates DNS, peer and TLS, and applies one deadline, with no redirects or hidden retries. 5, success returns only the status and the JSON body, or null for a declared empty status; a write whose answer is lost has an unknown outcome to inspect and reconcile before acting again.
svg.text: Keep the HTTP operation fixed; fill in values
The built-in weave-http@2.0.0 connector keeps connection policy, the
reviewed Action, and per-run input separate.
READ DOWN • Each arrow carries the result into the next step
1. Bind the connection
Fix the HTTPS origin, the authentication kind, secret handles
by slot, and the allowed destinations.
The operator controls network policy.
CONNECTION • Endpoint and credentials stay outside input
2. Publish the reviewed Action
Fix the method, path template, parameters, and statuses.
The method sets the side effect; a write is never retried.
Pin schemas, byte limits, and timeout.
Studio and the CLI check it offline; publishing checks again.
ACTION • The workflow cannot change this policy
3. Supply only declared values
Input may fill declared path, query, headers, and JSON body.
It cannot replace the origin, authentication, or
accepted-status policy.
INPUT • Values fit the published contract
4. Make one bounded native request
Validate the input, check authority, resolve scoped
credentials, then check authority again.
Validate DNS, peer, and TLS. One deadline covers
connecting, sending, and processing the response.
TRANSPORT • No redirects or hidden retries in v2
5. Validate success or record uncertainty
Success returns only the status and the JSON body,
or null for a declared empty status.
A write whose answer is lost has an unknown outcome:
inspect the incident and reconcile before acting again.
OUTCOME • Do not treat unknown delivery as safe retry
Keep policy and data separate
The native executor enforces the pinned operation. A workflow supplies
declared values within that boundary.

g.text: Keep deployment policy fixed and pass only the permitted per-run values.
